mainAirport.name: Brisbane Airport

runways.plain: new parallel runway (western, 3.3 km, opened July 2020)

mainAirport.curfew: No curfew - flights run 24 hours. At night, when wind and traffic allow, Airservices uses 'SODPROPS' (planes take off and land over Moreton Bay) to keep flights off homes.
mainAirport.notes: Two parallel north-south runways about 2 km apart: the legacy 01R/19L and the new 01L/19R (opened July 2020). The old cross runway 14/32 is closed (listed as CLOSED on OurAirports) and is not shown. Regular wide-body jets (A330, 787, 777, A350, A380) on international routes, plus 737/A320/A321 domestic jets and turboprops. The 2020 runway opening brought new flight paths and a big noise backlash; Airservices ran a Post-Implementation Review and a Noise Action Plan for Brisbane. Package 3 changes began 9 July 2026: northern arrivals moved further out over water (about 59,000 fewer people overflown incl. southern Bribie Island), southern arrivals redesigned (about 35,000 fewer), legacy-runway departures shifted south-east (about 44,500 fewer); Redcliffe, southern Moreton Bay, Bribie Island and Logan benefit most, while Bulimba (lined up with the new runway) sees no change and Russell Island gets a new path. Some changes still need CASA approval and may not happen until 2027. SODPROPS (Simultaneous Opposite Direction Parallel Runway Operations: arrivals and departures both over Moreton Bay) was about 3.8% of movements in early 2025 against a 5.3% target. Runway end coordinates from SkyVector (0.01-minute precision, about 20 m). Official map: engage.airservicesaustralia.com/nap4b?tool=map.

otherAirports.name: Archerfield Airport
otherAirports.note: Brisbane's main general-aviation airport, 12 km south of the CBD: flying-school light aircraft, charter turboprops and helicopters, with circuit training over Archerfield, Coopers Plains, Salisbury, Acacia Ridge and Algester. Busy daytime light-aircraft drone rather than jet noise.

otherAirports.name: RAAF Base Amberley
otherAirports.note: Australia's largest RAAF base, about 8 km south of Ipswich: F/A-18F Super Hornet and EA-18G Growler fighter jets plus C-17 and KC-30 heavy transports. Jet noise can be very loud (but irregular) in Ipswich, Yamanto, Deebing Heights, Ripley and Springfield-area suburbs under the circuit.

future.label: After independent parallel runway operations start (late 2027)
future.explain: Flight-path changes from July 2026 let Brisbane land planes on both runways side by side ('independent parallel runway operations'), which Airservices expects to use regularly from late 2027. Busy-period arrivals will then be split more evenly across both runways and their approach paths, so suburbs lined up with the new runway's approaches (such as Bulimba to the south) are likely to hear arrivals more often at peak times.

plans.name: Cross River Rail
plans.status: Under construction; services expected to start in 2029 (after testing)
plans.about: New 10.2 km line with 5.9 km twin tunnels under the Brisbane River and CBD, from Dutton Park to Bowen Hills, with new underground stations at Boggo Road, Woolloongabba, Albert Street and Roma Street. It also rebuilds eight southside stations (Salisbury to Dutton Park) and adds Gold Coast line stations at Pimpama, Hope Island and Merrimac.
plans.note: Dutton Park, Boggo Road, Albert Street and Roma Street points from station coordinates (Wikipedia); Woolloongabba, Exhibition and Bowen Hills points approximate.

plans.name: Logan and Gold Coast Faster Rail (Kuraby to Beenleigh)
plans.status: Under construction (main rail works started 2026; Kuraby station works underway, Loganlea relocation due 2027; full completion date not published)
plans.about: $5.75 billion project doubling the tracks from two to four along 20 km between Kuraby and Beenleigh, upgrading or relocating nine stations (Kuraby, Trinder Park, Woodridge, Kingston, Loganlea, Bethania, Edens Landing, Holmview, Beenleigh) and removing five level crossings. Means faster, more frequent Beenleigh and Gold Coast line trains, but more construction along the Logan rail corridor. Line points are approximate (station positions from general knowledge, not traced from official maps).

plans.name: The Wave - Direct Sunshine Coast Rail Line (Beerwah to Birtinya)
plans.status: Pre-construction; design contracts awarded 2026, major construction from early 2027, Stage 1 (Beerwah to Caloundra) targeted for 2032
plans.about: 26 km new heavy-rail line branching off the Sunshine Coast line at Beerwah: Stage 1 to Caloundra (19 km, new stations at Aura/Bells Creek and Caloundra) and Stage 2 to Birtinya (7 km, via Aroona, incl. ~1 km tunnel), linking to a future metro to Maroochydore and Sunshine Coast Airport. About 70 km north of Brisbane CBD. Line points are approximate (station positions from general knowledge, not traced from official maps).

plans.name: Coomera Connector Stage 1 (M9, Coomera to Nerang)
plans.status: Partly open: 4 km between Shipper Drive and Helensvale Road opened 3 Dec 2025; remaining 12 km to Nerang-Broadbeach Road under construction, finish promised 'by 2032'
plans.about: 16 km motorway east of the M1 on the northern Gold Coast, giving a second north-south route between Coomera and Nerang. Stage 2 north to Loganholme is still at business-case stage. Line points are approximate (station positions from general knowledge, not traced from official maps).

plans.name: Bruce Highway upgrade - Gateway Motorway to Dohles Rocks Road (Stage 1)
plans.status: Detailed design; construction expected to start late 2026
plans.about: $948 million rebuild of the Gateway Motorway / Bruce Highway / Gympie Arterial Road interchange at Bald Hills through to the Pine River, the first stage of widening the Bruce Highway north of Brisbane. Further business cases cover Anzac Avenue to Caboolture. Line points are approximate (station positions from general knowledge, not traced from official maps).
